User-grouped OOF requires explicit provenance: [GroupKFold](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold.html) keeps each group entirely within one fold. Recommended adaptation: persist `(category, user_id) → fold` before expanding histories into examples; retain user, prefix endpoint, and example ID in a separate feature-generation dataset. Preserve the diagnostic four-tuple contract by generating OOF features directly from `view.user_train`, or using dedicated fold-specific loaders. Anonymous batches cannot reliably recover ownership from sequence content: duplicated histories, truncation, shuffling, and repeated sampling defeat that approach. If provenance is unavailable, report fold-dependent diagnostics as unavailable.

For each held-out user, build transition/popularity tables exclusively from other folds. At position t, construct features from the prefix ending at `sequence[t]`, predicting `positive[t]`; exclude later sequence positions and padding. Apply identical truncation, normalization, smoothing, candidate scoring, and fallback rules during feature generation and inference. These are implementation recommendations consistent with research showing temporal leakage changes recommendation results; user grouping alone does not enforce global chronological causality. Preserve the benchmark’s fixed splits. [Leakage study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060)

[Standard stacking](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.ensemble.StackingClassifier.html) trains the combiner on OOF predictions and refits base estimators on all training data. For transition tables, that rebuild changes counts, coverage, and self-contribution for existing users. Normalized probabilities reduce scale changes but do not guarantee matching distributions. Recommended alternatives: retain fold-excluded tables and route known users through their saved fold at inference; or evaluate the all-user rebuild explicitly using permitted validation. Persist routing and table versions in predictor artifacts. Averaging folds also changes feature semantics and requires validation; never silently substitute all-user tables during diagnostics.
